To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) GaN films on sapphire are an excellent substrate for high-frequency SAW devices; (b) GaN SAW devices operate in a single mode at the fundamental frequency; (c) GaN S AW devices operate in the 5th through the 11th harmonic; and (d) SAW device fabrication is simplified by using a single-layer GaN film.
(1) GaN thin film SAW devices operating in the fundamental and harmonic frequencies can be designed and fabricated with simple, large, and low-loss interdigital transducers.
SAW devices on GaN films have been designed, simulated, fabricated, and characterized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, fabrication and measurement of SAW devices operating on GaN thin film/sapphire bilayers.
the design, fabrication, and measurement of SAW devices on GaN/sapphire.
the development of SAW devices on GaN thin film on sapphire substraties for applications in the 2 to 2.5 GHz range.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SAW devices operating up to 2 GHz on GaN films are feasible.
SAW devices fabricated from GaN films grown on sapphire substrats have a high frequency limit of about 2 GHz.
SAW propagation on GaN thin film is a viable technology for the development of high frequency SAW devices on GaN thin-films.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SAW devices operating on GaN thin-film bilayer are very attractive for high frequency applications.
GaN thin films can be used to realize high frequency SAW devices that are not affected by the substrate.
we have demonstrated the first SAW devices on MOVPE grown GaN thin films.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GaN thin films can be used to fabricate high frequency SAW devices.
the GaN/saphhire bilayer can be used as a substrate for the realization of SAW devices operating in the gigahertz range.
the GaN/silicon bilayer can be used for SAW devices operating from 1 to 2 GHz, with no need to grow GaN on silicon substrates.
